subject: science

entries: Alkanes: one CH₂ group apart: methane, ethane, propane and butane step up by one CH2 group each, sharing the general formula CnH2n+2 and the same family chemistry.
slots.label: Alkanes
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Functional groups change the family: the same carbon skeleton becomes an alcohol with -OH or a carboxylic acid with -COOH, and the functional group decides the reactions.
slots.label: Functional groups change the family
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Electrophilic addition to alkenes: the electron-rich pi pair of ethene attacks the slightly positive hydrogen of H-Br, the H-Br pair moves onto bromine, and bromoethane forms.
slots.label: Electrophilic addition to alkenes
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: SN1: the slow step comes first: the C-Br bond of a tertiary halogenoalkane breaks alone to give a planar carbocation, then OH- attacks fast, so rate = k[(CH3)3CBr].
slots.label: SN1
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: SN2: one step, backside attack: OH- attacks a primary halogenoalkane from the back as Br- leaves in a single concerted step, so rate = k[CH3Br][OH-].
slots.label: SN2
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: One route, three steps: ethene to bromoethane by addition, bromoethane to ethanol by substitution, ethanol to ethanal by partial oxidation - planned backwards by retrosynthesis.
slots.label: One route, three steps
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A common mistake: atoms sliding along the arrow: atoms stay put in a mechanism; the curly arrow tracks one electron pair from where it starts to where it ends.
slots.label: A common mistake
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Organic mechanisms in one page: addition is pi electrons attacking an electrophile, substitution is SN1's slow carbocation step or SN2's one concerted step, and synthesis chains known reactions.
slots.label: Organic mechanisms in one page
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A family of compounds with the same functional group and the same general formula, where each member differs from the next by one CH2 group, as methane to butane do for the alkanes, CnH2n+2.
slots.label: Homologous series
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The atom or group of atoms that decides a molecule's family and its characteristic reactions: -OH for alcohols, -COOH for carboxylic acids, C=O for carbonyl compounds.
slots.label: Functional group
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: An electron-pair acceptor: a species attracted to electron-rich regions such as a pi bond, for example the slightly positive hydrogen of H-Br in addition to ethene.
slots.label: Electrophile
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: An electron-pair donor: a species with a lone pair that it donates to form a new bond to carbon, for example OH- in the substitution of halogenoalkanes.
slots.label: Nucleophile
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A positively charged carbon intermediate with only six outer electrons: in SN1 it forms in the slow step when the C-Br bond breaks, and its planar shape lets the nucleophile attack from either side.
slots.label: Carbocation
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The arrow drawn in a mechanism to track one pair of electrons: it starts where the pair starts - a lone pair, a bond or a pi bond - and its head points to where the pair ends up.
slots.label: Curly arrow
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: JC H2 chemistry — organic: mechanisms, synthesis and the arrow language
